narrative: Years of reading terrain that wanted to kill you pay off in a way no drill ever taught you - a dip in the ground, a dead angle in the smoke, a line through the chaos that isn't safe exactly, but is THERE, and that's more than the field seems to be offering anyone else. You reach Aldous while Orin is still shouting for someone who can.

choices.label: Pull him and the wounded clear

effects.run_history: Reached Ser Aldous Fenn through a path only road instinct could find

narrative:
It isn't a farm and these aren't your neighbors, but the shape of the problem is exactly one you know - too much need, too little time, and a crowd that does better with clear direction than with none. You have soldiers who've never taken an order from a civilian in their lives moving wounded on your say-so within minutes.

@Orin: Where did you learn to do that? -no time to actually answer- Never mind. Keep doing it.

choices.label: Keep the triage moving while the battle turns

effects.run_history: Organized effective triage that saved lives on the Northern front

narrative:
The lines come back to you half-remembered, taught by someone who taught you many things you never expected to need this urgently. They flare pale and cold across the mud around the farmhouse, and for a handful of crucial seconds, the fire finds it cannot quite reach where Aldous and the wounded are sheltering.

It won't hold long. It doesn't need to hold long.

effects.run_history: Used an old elven ward to shield the wounded during battle

narrative:
Stone wants to fall a certain way if you understand its grain, and the farmhouse's foundation gives you exactly the leverage point you need - a controlled collapse that turns half a wall into cover instead of rubble, buying the wounded a shield that wasn't there a minute ago.

@Orin: That's - I don't even want to know how you knew that would work. It worked. That's enough.

narrative:
There isn't a version of this that looks entirely human, and you don't have time to care - one moment you're at the treeline, the next you're at the farmhouse, and Aldous is staring at you with an expression that will require an explanation later, if he survives long enough to demand one.

@Aldous, breathless: I am going to have SO many questions once we are not actively dying.

narrative:
You've seen this exact maneuver from the other side of it, once, in a war that isn't this one, for a company that isn't this one either. Knowing where it's weakest is muscle memory more than strategy - a gap that opens for exactly as long as it takes to matter, if someone already knows to look for it.

@Casswell, once it's over: Where in the Reaches did a wanderer learn to read a formation like that?
